system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Charles Schwab (SCHW) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Goldman Sachs Adjusts Price Target on Charles Schwab to $116 From $114, Maintains Buy Rating

BODY:
07:01 AM EST, 01/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Charles Schwab Corp (SCHW) has an average rating of overweight and mean price target of $116, according to analysts polled by FactSet.

(MT Newswires covers equity, commodity and economic research from major banks and research firms in North America, Asia and Europe. Research providers may contact us here: https://www.mtnewswires.com/contact-us)
</article>

<summary>
[SCHW relevance: primary | sentiment: positive]
Goldman Sachs raised its price target on Charles Schwab to $116 from $114, maintaining a Buy rating. Separately, FactSet notes an average overweight rating and $116 mean price target among polled analysts.
Key facts:
- Goldman Sachs price target raised to $116 from $114
- Goldman Sachs maintains Buy rating on SCHW
- FactSet analyst consensus: overweight, mean target $116
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article: invented facts,
wrong numbers, wrong direction (e.g. "rose" vs "fell"), wrong company, unattributed rumours stated as fact,
or speculative links to SCHW that the article does not make.
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about SCHW in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a SCHW analyst what matters, and represent how central SCHW really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for SCHW, and says so plainly if SCHW is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the SCHW angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores SCHW, or implies the article is about / important for SCHW when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": ["..."],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
